chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: The goatee, shaving and his chops
summary: He shaved the goatee after an infection before Korea; never had lip trouble.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: We were talking about the accoutrements around Bebop, with the glasses and the bowties, and you said that you had a goatee at one time.
Oh, yeah. I used to have a goatee. But I shaved it off, because when I was going to Korea, I had an infection down here on my chin, and the Japanese doctor told

me to shave all the hair off of it, and just put rubbing alcohol on my face. And I did that, and the next day it healed up. But I was going to (?) in Korea and so forth, I didn't want to get no stray varmints running around in my bloodstream. Heh-heh. So I said, "Well, I'd better hurry up and get that checked out."

But it was all right after that. I didn't have... But I couldn't wear hair no more. Every time I let it grow out, it would start breaking out again. So I figured out, "Who needs it? Let's cut it all off."
Because of course, the goatee became Dizzy's trademark.
and he claimed that the reason he had that was because he didn't want to shave too close to his chops. He said, "I want to protect my chops."
You never had any problems with shaving and playing.
No-no-no, I never had none of that. And I used to do it as high as it could go. I even hit a double high D one night, playing, and that's taking some energy, man. But I never did nothing to my lip.
